run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR", "FATAL"] }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log severity and re-run the query.

report.summary: The requested `terms: { level: ["ERROR", "FATAL"] }` query against index `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` returned 0 hits, but that zero is a schema artifact: the index has no `level` field. Its mapping contains only `@timestamp` (date), `msg` (text), `severity_num` (integer) and `svc` (keyword). The severity field is `severity_num`, and the documents show its encoding in the `msg` prefix: 3 = [INFO], 4 = [WARN], 5 = [ERROR], 6 = [FATAL]. Re-running the query on the correct field, `terms: { severity_num: [5, 6] }`, returned 8 hits (6 at 5 and 2 at 6), and an independent `match_phrase` search for `[ERROR]` / `[FATAL]` in `msg` also returned 8, so the two encodings agree. In the sampled documents the error/fatal lines are `[ERROR] DB timeout 1..6` at 06:42:01–06:42:06Z and `[FATAL] Disk full 1..2` at 06:43:01–06:43:02Z, all with `svc` = order-276. All counts are limited to the query window the tool enforced (2026-11-21T05:47:15Z–06:47:15Z), in which the whole 23-document index was matched; other windows were not sampled. No failure of the logged service was diagnosed here — this Run answered a log-count question only.

claims.text: The literal query `{"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}}` on index `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` returned total = 0 hits (relation eq), evaluated over @timestamp 2026-11-21T05:47:15Z–06:47:15Z.

The mapping of `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` contains exactly four properties: `@timestamp` (date), `msg` (text), `severity_num` (integer) and `svc` (keyword). No `level` field is mapped, so the zero hit count above reflects a non-existent field rather than an absence of error logs.

Reading all 23 documents matching `match_all` in the window (timestamps 06:42:01Z–06:45:10Z) shows `severity_num` maps to the `msg` prefix as: 3 = `[INFO]`, 4 = `[WARN]`, 5 = `[ERROR]`, 6 = `[FATAL]`, with `svc` = order-276 on every document.

Re-running on the correct severity field, `{"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}}`, returned total = 8 hits in the window, with terms buckets of 6 documents at severity_num 5 and 2 documents at severity_num 6 (sum_other_doc_count 0).

A cross-check by message text — `match_phrase` on `msg` for `[ERROR]` or `[FATAL]` with minimum_should_match 1 — also returned total = 8 hits in the same window, consistent with the 8 from `severity_num` in [5,6].

The 8 error/fatal level documents are `[ERROR] DB timeout 1` through `[ERROR] DB timeout 6` (severity_num 5, 06:42:01Z–06:42:06Z) and `[FATAL] Disk full 1` and `[FATAL] Disk full 2` (severity_num 6, 06:43:01Z–06:43:02Z), all from svc order-276; the remaining documents in that sample are 5 `[WARN] Slow query` (severity_num 4) and 10 `[INFO] Order placed` (severity_num 3).

Index `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` reported health green, status open, docs.count 23 and store.size 9.1kb at the moment of the query; the 23 documents matched in the 05:47:15Z–06:47:15Z window equal that total document count.

The zero result from the `level` query was considered as evidence that the index holds no ERROR or FATAL records. Rejected: the field `level` is not in the index mapping (properties are only @timestamp, msg, severity_num, svc), and once the severity is queried through `severity_num` in [5,6] the same window yields 8 error/fatal documents.

On the sampled data, `severity_num` is a compact numeric level scale (3 INFO, 4 WARN, 5 ERROR, 6 FATAL) rather than the OpenTelemetry SeverityNumber scale; this is consistent with all 23 documents but is not confirmed by metadata, since no metric or mapping documentation for `severity_num` values was read.
Query severity in this index via `severity_num` (5 = ERROR, 6 = FATAL) or via `match_phrase` on `msg`; do not use a `level` field, which does not exist in this mapping.

gaps: The elasticsearch_search tool forced a 1-hour window (2026-11-21T05:47:15Z–06:47:15Z) narrower than the authorized policy window (2026-11-20T06:47:15Z–2026-11-21T06:47:15Z); document contents and counts for the rest of the authorized day were not sampled, so the 8-hit count applies only to that 1-hour window.

severity_num values 1, 2 (and any above 6) were not observed in this index's documents, so whether other level values exist or are used elsewhere in the index is unknown; no metadata describing severity_num's value semantics was found.

The first attempt at the `level` terms query returned an INVALID_PARAMS parse error (unknown query [query]) because of a nested wrapper; it was re-sent correctly, so that particular error contributes no evidence about the index content.

No investigation of the logged failures themselves (e.g. `[FATAL] Disk full`, `[ERROR] DB timeout` in svc order-276) was performed or requested here: pod status, events, application runtime state and dependency health were not examined, so whether these log lines correspond to an active fault is unknown.
next_steps: If the log lines matter operationally, investigate svc order-276's pods (status, last termination reason, events) and its database/disk dependencies, and correlate with the 06:42–06:43Z timestamps observed in this index.
If a full-day count is required, run the same `severity_num` [5,6] query in successive 1-hour windows, since the search tool caps each call at a 1-hour time filter.
